subsystems.name: Platters
subsystems.role: the rotating disks that store data magnetically.

subsystems.name: Spindle motor
subsystems.role: spins the platters at constant speed, typically 5,400 to 15,000 rpm.

subsystems.name: Head and actuator assembly
subsystems.role: moves read/write heads across the platters to access tracks.

subsystems.name: Electronics and firmware
subsystems.role: controls data flow, error correction and head positioning.

subsystems.name: Enclosure
subsystems.role: keeps out dust and manages airflow or helium.

buildSteps.title: Make the substrate
buildSteps.detail: Aluminium alloy or glass blanks are machined and polished to near-atomic smoothness.

buildSteps.title: Deposit the magnetic media
buildSteps.detail: Thin cobalt-alloy films are sputtered onto the substrate, then coated with a carbon protective layer and a lubricant.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the heads
buildSteps.detail: Read sensors and write poles are built on wafers using thin-film lithography and etching, then diced into individual heads.

buildSteps.title: Build the head stack
buildSteps.detail: Heads are bonded to suspensions and mounted on the actuator comb in a cleanroom.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the drive
buildSteps.detail: Platters are stacked on the spindle motor, the actuator is installed, and the base is sealed.

buildSteps.title: Write servo patterns
buildSteps.detail: Precise position marks are written across every platter by specialised servo-writing equipment.

buildSteps.title: Test and format
buildSteps.detail: The drive is tested for capacity, speed and errors, then low-level formatted and its firmware loaded.

prerequisites.why: creates the magnetic recording layers with controlled thickness and grain structure.
giant and tunnelling magnetoresistance allow heads to sense tiny magnetic bits.
heads must fly nanometres above a disk spinning at high speed without touching it.
a single particle can damage the head-disk interface.

pathway.milestone: perpendicular magnetic recording in mainstream drives
pathway.unlocks: cheap bulk storage of tens of terabytes per drive.

pathway.milestone: energy-assisted recording (heat- or microwave-assisted) reaching the market
pathway.unlocks: higher areal density and drives beyond current capacity limits.

pathway.milestone: continued cost-per-terabyte advantage for cold and bulk data
pathway.unlocks: HDDs remain the economical tier behind solid-state drives.
